feedback.details: shared/sprint-count.ts line 10 uses `/^##\s*Sprint\s+\d+/gim` with `^` anchor and `m` (multiline) flag. Only headings starting at column 1 are matched.

Test in sprint-count.test.ts line 23-31 verifies exact contract scenario: '## Sprint 1' and '## Sprint 2' as headings plus 'builds on Sprint 3 features' prose returns count of 2. Blockquoted '> ## Sprint 3' tested separately at line 33-44, also correctly excluded. All tests pass.
Test 'counts standard line-start headings' (sprint-count.test.ts:5-21) has four '## Sprint N' headings at column 1 and asserts count is 4. Test passes.

conversation-logger.ts line 42-44 constructs timestampedName as `${ts}-${baseName}`, where ts comes from fileTimestamp() producing YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS format. Tests verify with TIMESTAMP_RE pattern. Finalize writes filename as `${timestampedName}.md`. Pattern verified by test execution.

Test 'resume does not overwrite prior logs' (conversation-logger.test.ts:104-130) creates two logs for same sprint/attempt with 1.1s delay and verifies both files exist with different timestamps and different content. Minor theoretical risk of same-second collision but practically sound.

harness-claude/contract.ts:34 passes logTimestamp to createConversationLog for contract-negotiation. Test at conversation-logger.test.ts:91-102 verifies filename matches TIMESTAMP_RE and contains 'sprint-3-contract-negotiation.md'. Passes.

All agent types use createConversationLog with timestamp: Generator (generator.ts:56), Evaluator (evaluator.ts:55), Planner (planner.ts:112), Documenter (documenter.ts:53), contract-negotiation (contract.ts:34). All go through fileTimestamp(). Tests cover Generator, Evaluator, Planner, Documenter, and contract-negotiation log types.

fileTimestamp() at logger.ts:58 uses getResolvedTimezone() which returns configuredTimezone set by setDisplayTimezone(). harness.ts calls setDisplayTimezone(config.tzDisplay) at startup. Same timezone logic used for both terminal output (timestamp()) and file timestamps (fileTimestamp()).

Fixed from round 0 (was 5/10). Now a single fileTimestamp() call is stored in a variable (e.g., generatorTs at sprint-attempts.ts:37, evaluatorTs at :149, negotiationTs at harness.ts:436, plannerTs at :108, documenterTs at sprint-success.ts:109) and used for BOTH the span name AND passed via logTimestamp to createConversationLog. The preGeneratedTimestamp parameter in conversation-logger.ts:39 ensures the same timestamp is used. Cross-referencing between spans and log files is now reliable.
Grep for '@anthropic-ai', 'claude-agent-sdk', 'openai', '@google' in shared/ returns zero matches. DI architecture boundary fully maintained.
fileTimestamp() defined once in shared/logger.ts:58. All call sites import and use this single function. No duplication of formatting logic anywhere in the codebase.

tests/sprint-count.test.ts has 9 tests covering: (1) standard headings counted (4→4), (2) inline prose not counted, (3) blockquoted headings not counted, (4) indented headings not counted, (5) backtick-quoted references, (6) zero headings, (7) case-insensitive, (8) varied whitespace, (9) complex acceptance criteria scenarios. All pass.

fileTimestamp() in logger.ts:58-84 has try/catch with two fallback paths: (1) if en-GB format doesn't match expected pattern, falls back to formatIsoAsFileTimestamp (line 79), (2) if timezone throws, logs debug warning and falls back to UTC-based ISO timestamp (lines 80-83). Function never crashes. Minor lint issues: unused 'err' variable (should be '_err') and string concatenation instead of template literal, but functionally correct.

evalResult.overallSummary: Sprint 1 successfully implements both features. The sprint-counting regex correctly uses ^ anchor with multiline flag and has comprehensive test coverage (9 tests). Timestamp log filenames work correctly with timezone support, graceful fallback, and DRY utility function. The Langfuse span alignment issue from round 0 is fixed — span names and log filenames now share a single pre-generated timestamp variable. All 474 tests pass. Minor lint issues (unused variable, string concatenation style, formatting) remain but do not affect functionality. All criteria score above threshold.
